title: Measurement Selection Strategies for Position Estimation in Indoor Environments
summary: Time-based indoor positioning techniques rely on multiple access points (APs) and measurements between the user equipment (UE) and the APs. In dense indoor environments, occlusion-induced non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation introduces significant delays in these measurements, thereby degrading position estimation accuracy. To address this challenge, this paper proposes measurement selection strategies to improve position estimation accuracy.
